messages:
maya: Heads-up — the raven-int4 canary we spun up overnight is showing a concentrated spike of funcall parse failures (structured output non-compliance). ETA: started ~03:20 UTC.

sam: ugh. numbers? are these streaming vs non-streaming?

maya: Canary-bot summary from the run:
canary-bot: canary run id=run-2026-03-21-03:20, model=raven-int4, total_invokes=18,742, parse_failures=412 (2.2%), malformed_json=298, truncated_stream=94, nonjson_suffix=20

liam: 2.2% is high for funcalls. correlated with long token lengths / big kvcache prefixes?

maya: quick sample of failing output (redacted prompt):
Expected schema: {"action": "string", "args": {"item_id": "string", "qty": integer}}

Actual model chunked stream (joined):
{"action": "create_order", "args": {"item_id": "sku-123", "qty": 3,}}

Note the trailing comma and then a truncated eos in several streams where the model emits a control char and we end up with a broken parse. Also some streams show split objects like '"args": {"items": [\n{"id": "a"' then stream ends and next chunk starts with ', "qty": 1}' which confuses our NDJSON rejoin heuristics.

ana: hypothesis: quantization (int4) changed emission patterns causing more control chars and earlier eos. Could also be KV prefix length shifting chunk boundaries.

sam: two probes: 1) run same canary on raven-int8 with identical prompts and compare parse-fail rate; 2) re-run raven-int4 with kvcache disabled to see if prefix-induced splits are main factor.

liam: also try running a postprocess json-sanitizer before parse (strip trailing commas, remove control chars, balanced-brace heuristics). That might reduce noise but we must know if it's masking a regression.

maya: action plan:
- A: run raven-int8 canary (same seed set) -> compare rates (sam)
- B: run raven-int4 canary with kvcache off -> compare rates (liam)
- C: enable json-sanitizer in probe pipeline for 1k samples and record how many parse_failures would be recovered (ana)
- D: collect top 50 failing prompts and timeline to see when failures started (maya)

ana: sanitizer snippet we can use:
function sanitize(s) { s = s.replace(/[\u0000-\u001F]/g, ''); s = s.replace(/,\s*([}\]])/g, '$1'); return s; }
We should log if sanitizer removes meaningful control chars.

sam: metrics: add parse_error_type dimension (trailing_comma, truncated_stream, nonjson_suffix, controlchar). Track prefix_length and first_k_tokens.

liam: experiment: on a 5k-sample subset run 3 variants in parallel: int4 w/ sanitizer, int4 w/o, int8 w/o. identical prompts/seeds. compare token emission diffs and parse failures. If int8 much better -> quantization-induced.

maya: pilot results (500 samples): raven-int8 parse_fail=1.0%, raven-int4 parse_fail=2.4%, raven-int4+sanitizer recovered 0.9% (net parse_fail ~1.5%). Sanitizer helps but doesn't close gap.

ana: implies both quantization changes and streaming boundary issues. Check failing cases with KV prefix >512 tokens.

sam: canary config tweak: add --log-prefix-len and --emit-chunk-boundaries flags to capture exact chunk split points per invoke. That'll show if structural token boundaries align with JSON brackets.

maya: concerned about masking regressions with sanitizer. Propose short-term fallback (sanitizer + retry) and rollback plan if int4 causes customer-facing issues.

liam: propose: implement sanitizer + one automatic retry with slight temperature drop and 'max_new_tokens=0' (regenerate suffix only) on parse_failures labeled truncated_stream or trailing_comma. If retry heals, mark auto-heal and surface telemetry. If not, fallback to int8 route for that session.

ana: ensure retry budget and latency SLO measured. Gate behavior behind feature flags per-customer.

sam: I'll own int8 vs int4 canary runs. Liam owns kvcache-off experiment and chunk-boundary logging. Ana runs sanitizer recovery eval and collects top-50 failing prompts. Maya does drift analysis and coordinates rollout decisions.

maya: quick command we used to start canary: ./tools/run_canary --id run-2026-03-21-03:20 --model raven-int4 --prompts dataset://funcall-canary-v2 --samples 5000 --emit-chunk-boundaries

liam: ping me for debug images with extra logging.

ana: collect token-level diffs for 200 recovered cases (int4 vs int8) for research micro-batch quant review.

maya: will make the tracking ticket and drop links here.

sam: :thumbsup:

liam: labels: severity=medium, dst=canary, owner=eng-ml-triage. Will update run when complete.

maya: thanks all. will follow up tomorrow with results.
